contradictions.why: Recommended start is 3-4 am in timing and 2-3 am in pro tips.

contradictions.fact: Route identity: North Face vs East Ridge

claims.says: North Face (Beckey-Schmidtke Route)
The East Ridge (Beckey-Schmidtke) route is the classic line
Summit push via the East Ridge couloir
800-foot, 50-degree ice couloir on the north face ... fourth-class rock climbing along the north arête to the summit
N/NE

contradictions.why: The same line is called the North Face/north arête in the name, beta and aspect but the East Ridge in the overview and itinerary.

claims.says: strong parties are back at camp 18-21 hours after leaving
a long summit day (10+ hrs round trip)
gains the top after roughly 10 hours of climbing

contradictions.why: Timing gives 20 h for the whole trip (7 h climb), the itinerary gives a 20 h summit day alone (33 h total, ~10 h to the summit), and partner requirements say 10+ h.
contradictions.internal_resolution: itinerary, totalNote and descent_text agree on an 18-21 h summit day; timing and partner_requirements understate it.

claims.says: 800-foot, 50-degree ice couloir
historically up to about 45-50 degrees
Steep snow/ice couloir climbing (reported up to ~50 degrees)
an 800 ft, 50-60 degree (one 70 degree step) snow/ice couloir
AI1-2 (early-season sections)

contradictions.why: The couloir is 45-50° in the beta, breakdown and partner requirements but 50-60° with a 70° step in the itinerary and max_angle.

claims.says: First rappel off the summit area on double ropes, capped near 30m.
Cited range is 10-12 rappels to 30m
parties describe roughly ten 60m rappels
Two 60m ropes for rappelling

contradictions.why: Rappels are ~30 m in the rappel table and count note but ten 60 m rappels in the descent text, with double 60 m ropes carried.

claims.says: Jun-Aug
Roughly Jun-Aug.
Mid-July through September is the reliable window.
Mid-July through September
a short practical window for the route roughly mid-July through September

contradictions.why: The season includes June and ends in August, while best_season, seasonal guidance and climate put the window at mid-July through September.
contradictions.internal_resolution: best_season, seasonal_guidance, climate and itinerary.cal ('July-August') agree the window starts mid-July; June in the season column is the outlier.

claims.says: Passenger cars can usually reach the trailhead in dry conditions
Road #34 is short (about 1 mile) and dead-ends at the trailhead.

Continue to the washout at 2.3 miles from the highway and park at Ruth Creek (elevation 2,156 feet). Hike the abandoned road beyond the washout for two miles to the Nooksack Cirque trailhead at 2,550 feet.
Nooksack Cirque Trailhead (Trail #750), elev 2200, distMi 0

contradictions.why: The road card says cars reach the trailhead on FR 34, while the approach says you park at the FR 32 washout and walk two miles to the 2,550 ft Nooksack Cirque trailhead; the waypoint puts that trailhead at the 2,200 ft parking spot.
contradictions.internal_resolution: approach, approach_variants and waypoint directions agree you park at the Ruth Creek washout; the road card is stale.

claims.says: it does not apply at the Nooksack Cirque (Ruth Creek) trailhead itself, where no pass is currently required
the parking pass at the road end and the park permit are two separate things you need at once

claims.says: alpine rock rack to 3 inches

contradictions.why: The rack goes to 3 in in the gear and rack fields but about 2 in in what-to-bring.

claims.says: crux moves around 5.4-5.5
Multi-pitch traditional leading up to 5.6
